cohort: The study included 36 women who had an intra-abdominal intrauterine device surgically removed by either minilaparotomy or laparoscopy at a tertiary referral center.
finding: Minilaparotomy was found to be a more cost-effective alternative to laparoscopy for the removal of intra-abdominal IUDs, with shorter operation times and fewer conversions to full laparotomy.
